summary:
ASTROCARE – Intelligent Health Monitoring Beyond Earth

Space exploration is an exciting step towards discovering the unknown, but the health of astronauts is one of the biggest challenges during long-duration space missions. Conditions such as microgravity, radiation, isolation and changes in the space environment can affect the human body in many ways.

We developed AstroCare with one simple goal: to help monitor and understand astronauts' health while they are far away from Earth.

AstroCare brings together health monitoring and interactive 3D human anatomy in one platform. It allows users to explore internal organs and monitor important health parameters related to the heart, brain, respiratory system and vision. Features such as ECG visualization, health dashboards, data analysis and mission-related insights help make complex health information easier to understand.

The platform also brings together space-health research and datasets to help track changes in astronauts' health over time. Through interactive visualizations and monitoring tools, we aim to make astronaut health information more accessible and meaningful.

We believe that space exploration is not just about reaching new destinations; it is also about making sure the people who take us there remain healthy and safe.

AstroCare – Caring for the people who explore beyond Earth.**
details:
ASTROCARE – Intelligent Health Monitoring Beyond Earth

Space exploration is a dream for humanity, but keeping astronauts healthy during long-duration space missions is a major challenge. Microgravity, radiation and isolation can affect different systems of the human body. Continuous monitoring is important to understand these changes and support safer missions.

To address this challenge, we developed AstroCare, a platform designed to bring astronaut health monitoring, interactive 3D anatomy and space-health research together in one place.

AstroCare allows users to explore the human body through 3D anatomical visualization and monitor important health parameters related to the heart, brain, respiratory system and vision. It also includes ECG visualization, health dashboards, telemetry tracking, data analysis, mission information and medical reports. NASA research data integration helps users explore scientific information relevant to astronaut health.

We developed the platform using React, JavaScript, Three.js and Tailwind CSS for the interactive frontend, along with Python, FastAPI and SQLite for backend services and data management. We also used GitHub for version control and Render for deployment. The project was developed using standard computer hardware and web technologies, without requiring specialized medical equipment.

What makes AstroCare different is its combination of interactive human anatomy and health monitoring. Instead of presenting health information only through numbers and charts, it helps users connect measurements with the actual organs and body systems they relate to.

While developing the project, we considered the challenges of long-duration missions, ease of use, clarity of health information, data reliability and the importance of distinguishing research data from simulated measurements.

Our aim is to make astronaut health information easier to explore and understand, and contribute towards safer and more sustainable human space exploration.

ASTROCARE – Caring for the people who explore beyond Earth.
